card.name: Words right after 'contraindicated' in labels
card.fires_on: The small word 'in' or 'who' right after 'contraindicated' (in patients) in contraindications sections. Also weaker on words that complete 'no two...' or 'cannot all be' style impossibility statements.

modes.label: Contraindication phrasing
modes.description: 'in' or 'who' following 'is contraindicated' or 'contraindicated in patients' at the start of a contraindications list.

modes.label: Impossibility statements
modes.description: A word in a sentence saying two things cannot both hold.
modes.example: That way<<,>> no two computers in the world can have

card.writes: It seems to push toward words meaning impossible or cannot, which fits a sentence about what must not happen.
card.plain: It lights up on the little word after 'contraindicated', where the label says who must not get the drug.
